explanation: The mesencephalic nucleus of the trigeminal nerve receives proprioceptive afferents from muscles of mastication and extraocular muscles. It is unique as a nucleus containing primary sensory neuron cell bodies (neural crest derived).
keyConcept: Mesencephalic nucleus receives mastication proprioception

explanation: The parasympathetic nucleus of the glossopharyngeal nerve is the inferior salivary nucleus. It provides parasympathetic innervation to the parotid gland via the otic ganglion.
keyConcept: Inferior salivary nucleus - parasympathetic to parotid

explanation: This matching tests cranial nerve nuclei: hypoglossal nucleus ( GSE) - tongue muscles; nucleus ambiguus (SVE) - pharynx/larynx; dorsal motor nucleus of X (GVE) - thoracic/abdominal viscera.
keyConcept: Hypoglossal nucleus supplies tongue muscles

explanation: The medial longitudinal fasciculus runs in the brainstem and receives input from the vestibular nuclei, interstitial nucleus of Cajal, and the superior colliculus. It coordinates head and eye movements.
keyConcept: MLF connects vestibular nuclei with eye movement nuclei

explanation: The somatic efferent column includes: oculomotor nucleus (III), trochlear nucleus (IV), abducent nucleus (VI), and hypoglossal nucleus (XII). These nuclei supply muscles derived from somites.
keyConcept: CN III, IV, VI, XII are somatic efferent nuclei

explanation: The nucleus solitarius is the visceral afferent column (receiving taste and visceral sensation), not the GVE column. GVE nuclei include Edinger-Westphal (III), superior/inferior salivary nuclei (VII/IX), and dorsal motor nucleus of X.
keyConcept: Nucleus solitarius is visceral afferent, not efferent

explanation: Special visceral afferent nuclei receive taste sensation. The nucleus solitarius (particularly its gustatory part) receives taste fibers from CN VII, IX, and X.
keyConcept: Special visceral afferent - taste fibers

explanation: Special visceral efferent (branchiomotor) column includes: trigeminal motor nucleus (V), facial nucleus (VII), nucleus ambiguus (IX, X, XI), and accessory nucleus (XI). These supply pharyngeal arch muscles.
keyConcept: SVE column - pharyngeal arch muscles

explanation: The tensor tympani and tensor veli palatini muscles are supplied by the trigeminal nerve (V3), not by nucleus ambiguus. All other pharyngeal arch muscles are supplied by nucleus ambiguus.
keyConcept: Tensor muscles supplied by CN V, not nucleus ambiguus

explanation: The hypoglossal nucleus is the only somatic efferent nucleus in the brainstem that supplies muscles of somite origin. Other somatic efferent nuclei (III, IV, VI) are in the midbrain/pons.
keyConcept: Hypoglossal nucleus is SE column in medulla

explanation: The abducent nucleus is not connected to the medial longitudinal bundle, which primarily coordinates eye movements between III, IV, and VI nuclei. Actually, it IS connected; perhaps another nucleus like the trochlear nucleus is being referenced.
keyConcept: Medial longitudinal bundle coordinates vestibular-eye reflexes

explanation: The special visceral efferent column supplies muscles derived from pharyngeal arches: mandibular arch (V) - muscles of mastication; VII - facial muscles; IX, X, XI - pharynx/larynx/sternocleidomastoid/trapezius.
keyConcept: SVE column supplies pharyngeal arch muscles

explanation: The facial nerve nuclei include: facial motor nucleus (SVE), superior salivary nucleus (GVE - parasympathetic), nucleus solitarius (SVA - taste), and mesencephalic nucleus of V (for facial proprioception).
keyConcept: Facial nerve has motor, parasympathetic, and taste nuclei

explanation: The nucleus that receives taste fibers is the nucleus solitarius (solitary nucleus), particularly its rostral/gustatory part. It receives SVA fibers from CN VII (via chorda tympani), IX, and X.
keyConcept: Nucleus solitarius receives taste sensation

explanation: The nucleus ambiguus supplies muscles of the larynx. However, all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid are supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve (branch of X).
keyConcept: Nucleus ambiguus supplies laryngeal muscles via X

explanation: This is an INCORRECT question about medial longitudinal bundle connections. The MLF does connect the vestibular nuclei with cranial nerve nuclei III, IV, and VI to coordinate eye movements.
keyConcept: MLF connects vestibular nuclei with eye movement nuclei

explanation: The trigeminal nerve (CN V) is the only pontine cranial nerve attached at the junction of the pons and middle cerebellar peduncle, supplying the second pharyngeal arch (mandibular arch) muscles.
keyConcept: CN V attached at pons-middle cerebellar peduncle junction

explanation: The mesencephalic nucleus of the trigeminal nerve is the first-order neuron for proprioception from muscles of mastication. Unique among sensory nuclei, it contains cell bodies of primary afferent neurons.
keyConcept: Mesencephalic nucleus of V is 1st neuron for mastication proprioception

explanation: This matching tests nuclei: facial nucleus - facial muscles; nucleus ambiguus - pharyngeal muscles; dorsal motor nucleus of X - visceral organs. All are branchiomotor or visceral motor nuclei.
keyConcept: Facial nucleus supplies muscles of facial expression

explanation: This matching tests cranial nerve nuclei columns: SE - somatic muscles (III,IV,VI,XII); SVE - pharyngeal arch muscles (V,VII,IX,X,XI); GVE - parasympathetic (III,VII,IX,X).
keyConcept: SVE column supplies pharyngeal arch derived muscles

explanation: This matching tests nucleus functions: hypoglossal - tongue movement; nucleus ambiguus - swallowing/phonation; dorsal motor X - parasympathetic to viscera; vestibular - balance; cochlear - hearing.
keyConcept: Nucleus ambiguus involved in swallowing and speech

explanation: The anterior spinal artery supplies the anterior 2/3 of the spinal cord: anterior horn, lateral horn, and anterior/lateral white columns. It does NOT supply the posterior columns.
keyConcept: Anterior spinal does not supply posterior columns

explanation: The gracile and cuneate nuclei are supplied by the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) and vertebral artery branches, not the anterior spinal artery.
keyConcept: Posterior spinal arteries supply dorsal column nuclei

explanation: Thrombosis of PICA affects the lateral medulla: cerebellum (ataxia), vestibular nuclei (vertigo/nystagmus), spinal trigeminal nucleus (face pain), nucleus ambiguus (dysphagia), and spinothalamic tract (contralateral body pain).
keyConcept: PICA thrombosis causes lateral medullary syndrome

explanation: Lateral medullary syndrome (Wallenberg) includes: ipsilateral face pain/temperature loss (spinal V), contralateral body pain/temperature loss (spinothalamic), dysphagia, hoarseness, ataxia, vertigo, nystagmus, Horner syndrome.
keyConcept: Lateral medullary syndrome includes vestibular symptoms
